newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 1.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Sri Lankan troops who captured the northern rebel stronghold of Kilinochchi over the weekend, find trail of destruction left behind by the rebels. The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) had destroyed public property, looted shops and blasted the town's telecommunications tower.

Troops who entered the long-time rebel-held town of Kilinochchi, find town empty of its civilian population. About 200,000 civilians from town had fled to safer ares south of Kilinochchi as the army began their advance on September 22.
Sri Lankan Suresh Joachim completes 1,000 hours of non-stop running, hoping to enter the Guinness Book of World Records.
Army arrests 47 people, including three women, in the northern Jaffna peninsula for allegedly cooperating with the LTTE.
Four policemen killed and 27 wounded when LTTE landmine hits a police convoy in the Jaffna peninsula.

Government Medical Officers Assocciation calls for people to donate blood for soldiers wounded in the latest offensive which enabled troops to take over the LTTE's stronghold of Kilinochchi. The army lost 269 soldiers while more than 300 were wounded in the offensive.
Private bus owners plan 30 percent price hike after government increased price of diesel and petrol last week.
